title: A train that passes over itself
text: To gain height here, the railroad goes round in a full circle and crosses over its own track. The circle is about 1,210 feet across, and a train climbing it gains 77 feet at a steady grade of around two percent. Any train longer than about 3,800 feet, roughly 56 boxcars, passes over itself going around.

s1.title: Tehachapi Loop
s1.quote: The Tehachapi Loop is a 3,779-foot-long (0.72 mi; 1.15 km) spiral, or helix, on the Union Pacific Railroad Mojave Subdivision through Tehachapi Pass ... rises at a steady two-percent grade ... a 1,210-foot-diameter (370 m) circle ... gaining 77 feet (23 m) in elevation. ... Any train that is more than 3,800 feet (1,200 m) long—about 56 boxcars—passes over itself going around the loop.

s2.title: Tehachapi Pass Railroad Line, National Historic Civil Engineering Landmark
s2.quote: The Tehachapi Loop ... 3,799-feet long, with a diameter of about 1,210 feet ... averages 2.2% in gradient across its 28-mile length
